Drives the three lifecycle transition commands on a managed-preset group -- forming to connecting to active to reconfiguring and back -- with formation-epoch assertions, a non-manager denial, and an illegal-transition denial.

Walks the observed activation condition across one formation and proves the status writer stored it: inactive with no coverage basis, initialising while dialing, active on the observed edge, and failed once a third session widens the planned edge set below the viable floor -- the band only the durable dwell clock can publish.

Exercises both legs of the activation criterion: a threshold group auto-activates from the evidence produced by its own establishment planning pass, and a deadline group with unconfirmed links fails formation below the floor -- typed outcome, attempt increment, and a parked DORMANT series at the attempt cap.

Drives the manager role end to end under an assigned policy: the non-manager owner is denied, the assigned manager establishes, removal passes duty to the next assigned member who completes the phase, and the zero-manager fallback blocks only manager-gated actions -- membership still works and joining the assigned member restores the manager.
No-browser API-v1 group create recipe covering the optional lifecyclePolicy request field: a normalized preset with overrides, and a create that omits it.

Debounced replanning on a managed group: a burst of replacing sessions extends the queued replan's window, the policy's maximum wait stops the extension, and the single replan covers the burst's last change.

Automatic formation triggers on a phased group: the plan trigger plans after its settle, the connect trigger dials the planned layout after the next settle, and a reconfigure that opens RECONFIGURING is dialed by the same trigger once its own replan publishes -- never the candidate it replaced, and with no application plan or connect command.
Presence stage triggers on a phased group: the second live member plans the group and dials the planned layout before either trigger's fallback.

A reconnection that misses the floor at its deadline lands back in ACTIVE rather than parking the series, because the attempt budget is not spent, and the accepted layout the match runs on is byte-identical afterwards.

Commanded replanning on a closed match group: a replacing session latches layoutStale with no automatic replan queued, reconfigure replans on command under a hold landing, and the promotion after connect and activate clears the obligation.

Composed match-preset behaviour: closed admission admits in FORMING and freezes outside it, deterministic election resolves the creator, blocked-until-active data NACKs in the lobby, full edge coverage activates at the all-or-nothing threshold and data flows, and a group with no confirmed edges exhausts both attempts below the floor and parks in DORMANT with the lobby still closed.

Composed drop-in-social-preset behaviour: immediate formation activates the group at creation, joins and rejoins admit instantly, no manager exists and lifecycle transitions stay server-owned, and application data flows from birth.

Pins the managed preset's manager-approval admission: uninvited joins park pending with invite-tier visibility, managers grant and decline, declined principals re-request, zero-manager groups recover through invite-and-accept, and a pending admission survives two formation-epoch advances before its grant lands.

Pins the admission binding phases: the member-count window closes joins in a group that never activates, the epoch-ms window denies after its deadline, and closed admits only while forming -- denying during establishment and activation, and staying closed once the spent series parks in DORMANT.

Pins the connect fence: after a second member's arrival replans the published layout, a connect naming a stale formation epoch is refused 409 group-connect-stale-epoch, a connect naming the replaced layout is refused 409 group-connect-planned-layout-superseded, neither refusal moves the group row, and the connect naming the current plan under the current epoch dials it.

Pins the preActivationAppData gate: under blocked-until-active a room-scoped WS app-data send is NACKed unauthorized before activation and never reaches other members, then flows end to end once the manager activates the group.

No-browser three-server convergence test for immutable RTC topology revisions and PostgreSQL-backed WebSocket fanout. The group pins the hold reconfigure landing so the only group-state.event envelopes are the two mutations it commits: under apply, the route-less applyPlannedLayout promotion emits a third envelope that the exact-revision assertions would consume. Route-less promotion is covered by api-v1-state-topology-churn.

Bounded three-server load recipe with 12 clients contending across two groups and disconnect/reconnect presence churn. Both groups take the default apply reconfigure landing and the recipe issues no lifecycle command, so the accepted layout each closing reconfigure lands can only have come from the route-less applyPlannedLayout promotion.
Three-server state-write convergence gate for bounded membership, reused-session fencing, topology config receipts, and causal history.
Three-node canonical HTTP idempotency contract gate for replay, conflict, isolation, single-use auth, CRDT, admin, topology, and exact durable completion.
Three-server CRDT AppInbox gate for authenticated append, committed reply, durable fanout, and catch-up.

Three-node reading of the stage-transition metrics bucket: a managed group is planned, dials itself on the connect trigger and is activated, with admin group-formation metrics read on every node before and after, because the counter is process-local and the AppInbox is claimed by any node.
Diagnostic CRDT append and replay evidence from 10 through 30 durable updates.
Diagnostic CRDT append and replay evidence from 100 through 120 durable updates.
Diagnostic CRDT append and replay evidence from 480 through 500 durable updates.
Opt-in three-server PostgreSQL gate with 100 independently authenticated clients across five contended groups.
Formation-burst baseline small tier: 6 clients join one group in a burst, converge, then hold a ~60s steady-state heartbeat window while admin group-formation metrics are captured at T0/T1/T2.
Formation-burst baseline medium tier: 20 clients join one group in a burst, converge, then hold a ~60s steady-state heartbeat window while admin group-formation metrics are captured at T0/T1/T2.

Managed threshold burst medium tier (N=20): 20 clients join a preset:managed phased group, the creator-manager connects the published layout, readiness holds at zero observed edges, a planned-edge RTT burst covers the mesh, and activation fires only at threshold (outcome activated, observedRate 1).

Opt-in formation-burst baseline large tier: 50 clients join one group in a burst against the three-server PostgreSQL cluster, converge, then hold a ~60s steady-state heartbeat window while admin group-formation metrics are captured per server at T0/T1/T2.

Managed threshold burst large tier (N=50): 50 clients join a preset:managed phased group, the creator-manager connects the published layout, readiness holds at zero observed edges, a planned-edge RTT burst covers the mesh, and activation fires only at threshold (outcome activated, observedRate 1).

Opt-in phase-4 churn stream large tier: 50 clients form one group against the three-server PostgreSQL cluster and converge, then a sequential join/leave churn stream runs six cycles with settle delays longer than the coalesced recompute debounce, followed by a ~60s steady-state heartbeat window; admin group-formation and rtc-topology metrics are captured per server at T0/T1/T2/T3 so the churn window isolates per-change replan, publication, and egress quantities.
No-browser API-v1 scoped application/workspace isolation recipe.
No-browser API-v1 OpenAPI auth contract for scoped graph and topology management endpoints.

No-browser API-v1 admin operations auth denial, admin overview success, and OpenAPI contract coverage. The scoped admin reads are pinned against two scopes at once: one nothing has ever written, which must answer all-zero, and one this recipe populates with exactly one group, which must answer one -- the pair is what distinguishes a read that filters by scope from a read that ignores its scope, and the unscoped variants must omit the scope echo. CRDT integrity and debug export are driven over a document that was never written, which pins that redaction is opt-OUT: only an explicit redactPayloads false disables it. metrics/reset is deliberately NOT exercised here -- it resets the server-wide RTC-topology and group-formation metric owners that the formation burst and churn recipes read on the same server, so it needs its own profile.
No-browser API-v1 admin support auth denial, explicit QueueBox-key explanation, constrained request warning, and OpenAPI contract coverage.
No-browser API-v1 black-box operator token and agent-session ticket lifecycle coverage.
No-browser API-v1 authenticated WebRTC ICE configuration coverage.
No-browser API-v1 SPA statistics missing-auth denial, non-member group denial, scoped success reads, and OpenAPI contract coverage.
No-browser API-v1 durable CRDT catch-up authorization: non-member room denial, non-owner principal denial, and unauthenticated denial.
No-browser API-v1 presence lease bounding: group and client sessions reject far-future connect/heartbeat timestamps while normal connects still succeed.

No-browser API-v1 cross-application WS isolation: the same groupId in two applications delivers group frames only inside each scope, proven with positive same-scope controls and expect.absent negative waits.
No-browser API-v1 read-your-writes: after a presence connect, an http.poll-until floor read must show the session in activeSessions under compatible-complete, not merely satisfy the causal floor.

No-browser API-v1 cross-principal isolation: two principals in the same workspace without a shared group prove own client-state.snapshot delivery, then expect.absent proves neither socket ever receives a frame targeted at the other principal (requires damped group formation).
No-browser API-v1 negative shape: group stats return the owner block to the owner (path-resolution positive control) and omit it for a plain member, asserted via the missing-observation sentinel.
Dry-run signaling-only two-peer chat recipe expansion.
Live signaling-only provider check. Requires a signaling server URL.

No-browser API-v1 late-joiner overlay read-through: after formation, a member who joins without a presence transition reads the current server overlay from GET topology immediately, with the served version equal to the pre-join publication (no new publication awaited).

No-browser API-v1 reconnect resync: a client drops WS, misses a fingerprint-relevant group update and its publication, reconnects on a fresh socket, receives the unicast topology hydration push, and converges through the floored snapshot read and the topology read-through.

No-browser API-v1 join-admission limiting: one probe principal fires 70 rapid upsert-self join attempts at a single open group so the per-principal window (60/min) actually engages, then a deterministic over-limit request must answer 429 with Retry-After: 60 while the founder still joins the same group successfully (per-principal isolation, no group-wide collateral).

No-browser API-v1 ban governance: a banned member cannot shed the ban through the self-service member upsert. Self status 'left' and a self rejoin both answer 403 member-banned while the row stays banned, and only the founder's unban returns the principal to a rejoinable state.

No-browser API-v1 ownership transfer: the highest-authority group mutation, whose denial paths no recipe reached. A plain member is denied forbidden-role, a non-member target is the compute's 400 rather than the contract's 404 (an open contract defect the plan records, not a behaviour to keep), an accepted transfer swaps both roles at once so the old owner becomes admin and a read-back proves the swap was persisted, and a sole owner targeting themselves is denied last-owner by the governance policy before the compute's self-transfer no-op can run. Each denial pins the message that separates its own rule: forbidden-role is returned both by the generic governance check and by the transfer-only check.

No-browser API-v1 governance authority: ban, unban, remove and role promotion had owner-happy-path coverage only. A plain member is denied forbidden-role on all three governing routes, an admin may govern a regular member but neither the owner nor another admin, and a removed member is denied by member-removed rather than member-banned. Each denial pins the message that separates its own rule, and each accepted mutation pins the roster it produced -- the unban returns the member to 'left', not 'active'.

No-browser API-v1 invite revocation and expiry: six recipes drive the invite routes and none asserts a single invite denial. A stranger, a revoked invitee on the accept route and that same invitee on the join route all reach the single not-invited branch, so group-invite-required is observed from three different member states rather than one; only the expired invitee carries its own code and message. A live invite still admits, so the denials are not a route that refuses everyone.

No-browser API-v1 browser-director appointment: the route no recipe calls, and every denial it raises shares one code so only the reason separates them. A non-member, a member without an active room session, a plain member while an owner is online, and a second member against an active fallback director are each refused with the reason that names the branch. Each accepted appointment advances the director epoch and the metadata version by exactly one, pins the heartbeat TTL default, and leaves the group fields and the seeded metadata entry it must not touch unchanged.

No-browser API-v1 code-protected admission: group-code-required and group-code-invalid are returned by no recipe in the corpus. A code group refuses a join carrying no code and a join carrying the wrong one, the current code admits, a rotation invalidates the old code while the new one admits, and an expired code is refused even for a principal who is already an active member. Rotation is refused for a non-member and again for an active regular member -- the server returns the same envelope for both, so only the second probe pins the owner/admin rule. Both sides normalise the code identically, so the typed form and the returned form are interchangeable.

No-browser API-v1 invite admission through the group join route. The self-upsert member route reaches the same two denial codes but is registered separately, so covering one proves nothing about the other and this recipe drives the join route only. Also pins that the reserved inviteToken field cannot admit anyone, because nothing in the server ever sets the token it is compared against.

No-browser API-v1 business status: group-archived and group-deleted are returned by no recipe in the corpus. An archived group refuses new joins while its own members can still read, and is terminal at the route -- assertCanUpdateGroup denies the owner and a plain member alike, so the lifecycle refusal is raised ahead of the role check and the group can be neither revived nor deleted. Deletion is reachable only from active, each transition stamps its own audit entry and clears the other, and a deleted group refuses the read path and the mutation path with the message and the envelope that separate them.

No-browser API-v1 group limits: group-not-active and member-session-limit-reached are returned by no recipe in the corpus. A group whose clock has passed still stores status active and stays readable, yet refuses a join with the message that separates an expired clock from a non-active status; a second group carrying a future clock admits through the same guard, so the comparison is pinned rather than the mere presence of the field. A second session for one principal trips maxSessionsPerMember, which is a strict greater-than so a cap of one refuses only the second.

No-browser API-v1 group-state delta contents: the corpus proves delta frames arrive and never reads what is in them. removedSessionIds is the one reachable removal set, populated only by the self-disconnect route, and the disconnecting session never sees its own removal, so a second peer observes it. removedMemberPrincipalIds is a hard-coded empty literal no mutation can populate. Removing a member who holds live presence drops the session from activeSessionIds while naming nothing in either removal set. Each delta binds to its own mutation by event.requestId through expect.decodeJsonPaths.

No-browser API-v1 overlay topology publication: nothing in the corpus reads an overlay frame body. A published overlay.topology broadcast is compared field for field against the authoritative HTTP topology read at the same version; the row is written in the transaction that publishes, so the equality is a real invariant. The frame is selected by its own degreeLimit through expect.decodeJsonPaths, which separates it from the unicast hydration frame every socket receives on connect, and both members must receive the same body rather than a body each.

No-browser API-v1 lifecycle command race: no recipe in the corpus places a lifecycle command inside a parallel block. Two members command plan on one group at once, released together by a barrier so the contention is real rather than adjacent. Both must succeed -- planned to planned is the idempotent cell, so the loser is a no-op and not a conflict -- and the formation epoch must have advanced exactly once, however many principals asked.

No-browser API-v1 admission decision race: grant and decline are covered sequentially and never raced. Both are issued against the same pending principal at once behind a barrier, neither group asserting a status because which decision wins is the server's to decide, and the seat must then have settled on exactly one outcome.

No-browser API-v1 cluster lifecycle over a non-primary socket. Exactly one lifecycle recipe runs against three nodes today. Group setup is written on primary and secondary only, then the connect command is served by the tertiary node, which wrote none of it, fenced on the layout the other two produced, and both writing nodes must read the result back. The sockets are opened against RALLAR_WS_BASE_URL_SECONDARY, which the runner exports and no recipe in the corpus has referenced, and the connect delta is bound to the tertiary command by its own requestId. Which node executed the entry is deliberately not asserted: those counters are process-local.

No-browser API-v1 admin authorization boundary: the whole admin surface against an authenticated non-admin principal. One conceptual denial reaches the client in four shapes and two are wrong -- the CRDT admin reads answer 400 rather than 403, and that guard is the only authorization on those routes and has never been executed by any test, which all run with requireAuth false; the admin operations mutations answer 500 api-mutation-unexpected rather than 403 because the guard throws a statusless Error. Every denial is compared exactly, so a refusal leaking a diagnostic payload would fail.

No-browser API-v1 activation clock decay: the evidence-expiry heartbeat is asserted nowhere. The observed edge is reported with an already-stale createdAtEpochMs, which is client-supplied and never compared to now at write time, so it still activates the group and then decays it when the heartbeat re-reads past the freshness window. A count wait pins exactly two status writes, so a clock that never fires and one that republishes on every observation both fail. Read off the group row, since only a writer can put the degraded band there.

No-browser API-v1 reconfigure landing concurrency: reconfigureLanding apply has no coverage anywhere in the corpus, since every recipe that sets it pins hold, so a reconfigure has never been observed landing. Two reconfigures asking for different degree limits are released together by a barrier, so neither is skipped as unchanged and neither is merely adjacent. The row settles on exactly one of the two requested limits and the layout version must have advanced.

No-browser API-v1 activation command race: a latecomer join against the activation that closes the lobby, released together by a barrier. Activation is driven manually on purpose, because the criterion has no HTTP surface and racing it would be settle-sequenced rather than a parallel block. Neither side asserts an outcome; what is required is that the activation was answered and the lobby is closed whichever way the race went.

No-browser API-v1 CRDT admin write surface: backup-export, rebuild-projection and erase need a CRDT admin session and no recipe drives their success path, only the invalid-mode and invalid-lifecycle rejections. Backup-export of an absent document must be the documented null rather than an error, the two write routes must answer the same way for the same absent document, and the read surface must still answer afterwards.

No-browser API-v1 graph diagnostic reads: the two GET routes the OpenAPI assertion covers and no recipe requests. Both are cache state machines with three refresh modes and the corpus pins none of them: never on a cold cache is the only 404 for a group that exists, if-missing computes once and then serves the same snapshot, and always must advance a version the compute itself never advances. Also pins includeMeasured defaulting to absent, an unknown refresh mode rejected by the route rather than the schema, and the scoped global graph as a separate cache entry.

No-browser API-v1 presence lease expiry against a lifecycle-managed group. The corpus asserts the lease bounds and never the expiry: disconnectReason appears in no recipe and the internal expired reason has never been observed. One member takes a lease that lapses seconds later, the group is driven to connecting, and the 60s reconciliation sweep is allowed to fire. The sweep deletes the expired row rather than marking it disconnected, so exactly one session must survive and it must be the other member; membership and lifecycleState must be untouched, and the expired member must be able to take a fresh lease without rejoining. Waits out one full sweep interval.

No-browser API-v1 group event cursor paging across three nodes. The corpus requests /events/page twice and asserts only its status: no limit, no cursor, and hasMore is read nowhere. A bounded page is opened on the primary and continued on the secondary and again on the tertiary, because the cursor is three durable event columns rather than node-local state; the pages must not overlap and the remainder must end. Two silent fallbacks are pinned as well: a partial cursor is dropped rather than rejected, so a caller sending only the event id re-reads page one forever, and a zero or non-numeric limit falls back to the default 100 instead of answering 400.

No-browser API-v1 group governance fencing across three nodes. Ban, unban, removal and the two admission decisions are each written on one node and enforced or read back on the nodes that never saw the write; group snapshots are served through a node-local cache, so a fence that is only correct on the writing node is the regression this catches, and no existing recipe crosses a node with any of these. Every denial names its code rather than its status: member-banned on both non-writing nodes, member-removed after a removal written elsewhere, and an unban that lets the rejoin through on a third node. The admission half parks a request on one node, decides it on another, and requires the decision visible on the node that parked it.

No-browser API-v1 reconnect hydration across a lifecycle stage change and across nodes. api-v1-group-state-reconnect-resync already drops a socket, mutates the group and reopens, but it reopens on the same node and the group never changes stage. Here the socket is dropped during connecting, the group is activated from the tertiary while the client is offline, and the client reconnects on the secondary with a fresh ws-ticket for the same session. The reconnect must be hydrated by a unicast overlay.topology frame from a node that never held the socket it replaces, a floored read on the third node must reach the post-change revision, and the layout version must not have moved: a stage change is not a replan.

No-browser API-v1 activation degraded band from partial coverage, the arm api-v1-activation-clock-decay cannot reach: with one planned edge a lapsed observation is a rate of zero and the band is failed, not degraded. Three members plan two or three edges and exactly one is ever reported, named by reading the manager's own next hop out of the published layout so the recipe never guesses the topology. minimumViableRate 0.25 against successRate 0.95 puts a single observed edge above the floor and below success whatever the planner chose. degraded is a dwell-held band so one instantaneous reading cannot reach it, the group must still be connecting because partial coverage is not activation, and the formation view must agree with the group row.
